title: Onboarding copy

body.text: Good onboarding gets the user to the
aha moment — the point where they first see the product's value — as fast as possible
. Every screen in the way is a chance to lose the user, so the copy must move them forward, not explain every feature.

example: "A notes app: instead of a 5-screen tour → open straight to 'Write your first note' with a text field right there"

title: Writing onboarding with Claude

body.text: what the product's aha moment is, then have it design the shortest path to that point
— with copy for each step that prompts action, not just explanation.

example: "Product: a group expense-sharing app / aha: seeing how much each friend owes, calculated automatically → design a 3-step onboarding with copy"

options.text: The point where the user first sees the product's value

question: What should good onboarding be like?

options.text: Get to the aha moment as fast as possible

question: What should onboarding copy be like?

options.text: As long and detailed as possible

question: When writing good onboarding copy, what should you focus on?

options.text: Explaining every feature at length right away
Getting the user to the first value quickly and clearly

question: What does good onboarding help with?

options.text: Helps the user get started successfully and stay
